extracted.intended_audience: Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs), Long-Term Care Hospitals (LTCHs), hospital administrators, Medicare providers, and stakeholders preparing comments on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and substantive standards for the Federal Register proposed rule covering the Frontier Community Health Integration Project (FCHIP) demonstration extension and proposed FY2027 changes to the LTCH PPS, including eligibility, payment waivers, budget neutrality methodology, and MS-LTC-DRG classification/update policies. Useful for preparing regulatory comments or compliance actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver authority for demonstration projects (section 123(i) of Pub. L. 110-275)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary may waive such requirements of titles XVIII and XIX of the Act as may be necessary and appropriate for the purpose of carrying out the demonstration project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS relied on this waiver authority to waive Medicare payment rules in order to implement enhanced payment for telehealth, SNF/NF beds, ambulance services, and home health services for participating CAHs; waivers were formulated with the goal of increasing access to care with no net increase in costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to participate in FCHIP demonstration extension (section 129 of Pub. L. 116-260)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the 10 CAHs that participated in the initial period of the FCHIP Demonstration are eligible to participate during the extension period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Among the eligible CAHs, some may elect whether to participate in the extension period and may change the number of interventions/payment waivers they participate in; CMS may accept and approve CAH intervention and payment waiver updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions available under FCHIP demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Four distinct interventions were identified for CAH participation: telehealth services; skilled nursing facility/nursing facility (SNF/NF) beds expansion; ambulance services; and home health services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments and payment waiver provisions only apply if the CAH is a participant in the associated intervention; CAHs may participate in more than one intervention; in initial and extension periods none participated in home health intervention in the selected cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telehealth services intervention payment modifications and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS waives section 1834(m)(2)(B) (originating site facility fee) and modifies it to reimburse participating CAHs 101 percent of reasonable costs for overhead, salaries and fringe benefits when they serve as the originating site; CMS also waives section 1834(m)(2)(A) to permit 101 percent cost-based reimbursement to CAHs billing for distant-site practitioner professional services when practitioners reassign billing rights to the CAH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS does not fund or reimburse for purchase of new telehealth equipment; CAHs billing under Standard or Optional Payment Method II may be reimbursed at 101% of reasonable costs when conditions described are met; CMS does not waive other provisions of section 1834(m), including scope of Medicare telehealth services under 1834(m)(4)(F). Payments to distant-site physicians/practitioners who have not reassigned billing rights continue under the physician fee schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambulance services intervention payment waiver and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS waives 42 CFR 413.70(b)(5)(i)(D) and section 1834(l)(8) to permit participating CAHs (or CAH-owned entities) to be paid 101 percent of reasonable costs for ambulance services regardless of whether another provider/supplier is located within a 35-mile drive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This waiver does not authorize cost-based payment for new capital (e.g., vehicles) associated with ambulance services and does not modify other Medicare rules regarding ambulance service provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNF/NF beds expansion intervention waivers and payment
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS waives 42 CFR 485.620(a), 42 CFR 485.645(a)(2), and section 1820(c)(2)(B)(iii) (limits CAHs to 25 inpatient beds) and waives section 1820(f) to permit participating CAHs with swing bed approval to maintain up to 10 additional beds (total 35) used only for nursing facility or skilled nursing facility level of care; CMS would pay participating CAHs 101 percent of reasonable costs for SNF/NF services furnished in the 10 additional beds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The waiver allows use of additional beds only for SNF/NF level of care and applies only if the CAH has swing bed approval; it does not broadly remove other inpatient limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal and selection principle: maintain demonstration budget neutrality on program terms
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS selected CAHs with the goal of maintaining the budget neutrality of the demonstration on its own terms, meaning demonstration savings (from reduced transfers/admissions) would offset any increased Medicare payments resulting from the demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the small size and uncertainty of projected utilization/costs, CMS adopted contingency policies (described below) to ensure budget neutrality if the demonstration increases net costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality statutory requirement (section 123(g)(1)(B) of Pub. L. 110-275)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate payments made by the Secretary must not exceed the amount the Secretary estimates would have been paid if the demonstration project was not implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS interprets the statutory language as permitting recoupment mechanisms across a range of payment sources and finalized a policy to recoup additional expenditures attributable to the demonstration by reducing payments to all CAHs nationwide if increases are not sufficiently offset elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality contingency policy: recoupment across all CAHs if excess expenditures occur
rubrics_metrics.description: If analysis shows increases in Medicare payments under the demonstration are not sufficiently offset by reductions elsewhere, CMS would recoup additional expenditures attributable to the demonstration through a reduction in payments to all CAHs nationwide rather than only participating CAHs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS justified this approach by the small scale of the demonstration and the design to test innovations affecting the CAH provider category; finalized policy includes recoupment within one fiscal year in the event the extension period is found not to have been budget neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality timing: recoupment within one fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS finalized a policy that any excess costs identified for the demonstration extension period would be recouped within one fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explained that a one-year timeframe is more efficient for concluding operational requirements (analyzing claims/cost reports/other data) to adjudicate the budget neutrality payment recoupment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCHIP budget neutrality analytical approach: data components
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget neutrality analytical approach incorporates two major data components: (1) Medicare cost reports; and (2) Medicare administrative claims (and enrollment data) for beneficiaries who received demonstration intervention services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS computed cost of the demonstration for each fiscal year using submitted cost reports for participating CAHs and administrative claims; claims analysis would be reconciled using audited cost report data; final results determined once complete data are available for each CAH for the extension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of statistical modeling (Difference-in-Difference regression) to estimate demonstration impact
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS developed a DiD regression analysis to estimate demonstration expenditures and compute impacts by comparing cost data for demonstration and non-demonstration groups across baseline and performance periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DiD would compare direct costs and potential downstream effects (including savings) of intervention services during baseline vs performance periods for both groups; used to capture full impact of interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of CAH-specific demonstration costs using 'as submitted' cost reports
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS would estimate demonstration costs using 'as submitted' Medicare cost reports for each hospital's financial fiscal year participation within each demonstration extension performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each CAH has its own Medicare cost report end date applicable to the 5-year period; cost reports gather costs, revenues and statistical data on the provider's financial fiscal period; final budget neutrality results require complete data availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy to follow initial period methodology for extension period, with possible updates
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS's policy for implementing the 5-year extension follows the same budget neutrality methodology and analytical approach as the demonstration initial period but may update/modify the methodology upon receiving extension-period data to better capture full impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While expecting to use the same methods, CMS reserves the right to update/modify the methodology/analytical approach based on extension period data.

rubrics_metrics.name: No FY 2027 budget neutrality payment offset proposed
rubrics_metrics.description: For the FY 2027 proposed rule, CMS does not propose to apply a budget neutrality payment offset to payments to CAHs in FY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects an anticipated approach to assessing financial impact pending receipt of full extension-period data; the policy would have no impact on any national payment system for FY 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria to qualify as an LTCH for payment under LTCH PPS (§412.23(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify to be paid under the LTCH PPS, a hospital must have a provider agreement with Medicare and have an average Medicare inpatient length of stay of greater than 25 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medicare Advantage plan discharges and site neutral payment rate discharges are excluded from the average length-of-stay calculation for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2015; these regulatory requirements implement section 1886(d)(1)(B)(iv) of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospitals excluded from LTCH PPS payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain hospitals are paid under special payment provisions and therefore are not subject to LTCH PPS rules: Veterans Administration hospitals; hospitals reimbursed under State cost control systems approved under 42 CFR part 403; hospitals reimbursed under specified demonstration projects; nonparticipating hospitals furnishing emergency services to Medicare beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are described in §412.22(c) and implement statutory/payment exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on charges to beneficiaries under LTCH PPS (§412.507)
rubrics_metrics.description: An LTCH may not bill a Medicare beneficiary for more than the deductible and coinsurance amounts as specified under §§409.82, 409.83, and 409.87, and for items/services under §489.30(a); exception: if Medicare payment was for a short-stay outlier (SSO) case and payment was less than full LTC-DRG amount due to insufficient coverage, the LTCH may charge for services delivered on uncovered days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations were amended to limit charges on discharges paid at the site neutral payment rate and to address blended payments during transitional periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual update requirement for MS-LTC-DRG classifications and relative weights (§412.517(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: MS-LTC-DRG classifications and relative weights must be updated annually; for FY2027 CMS proposes updates consistent with the proposed MS-DRG changes effective Oct 1, 2026 through Sept 30, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the classification system is structurally identical to the MS-DRGs used under IPPS, relative weights under LTCH PPS reflect LTCH patient resource use; for FY2027 there would be 768 MS-DRG/MS-LTC-DRG groupings under the proposed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data elements used for MS-LTC-DRG assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases are classified into MS-LTC-DRGs for payment based on six data elements: principal diagnosis; additional or secondary diagnoses; surgical procedures; age; sex; discharge status of the patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ASC X12 5010 claims, up to 25 diagnosis codes and 25 procedure codes are considered for MS-DRG assignment (one principal diagnosis and up to 24 secondary diagnoses for severity determinations).

rubrics_metrics.name: HIPAA transaction and coding standards for claims and coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must use ASC X12 5010 standards for institutional health care claims (837) and applicable operating rules; HIPAA requires use of adopted medical data code sets for transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On or after Jan 1, 2012, entities are required to use ASC X12 5010 standards (and errata) for institutional claims; upon discharge LTCHs must assign diagnosis and procedure codes from ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS (required Oct 1, 2015); additional coding instructions/examples are published in AHA's Coding Clinic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare Code Editor (MCE) screening and GROUPER assignment process
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicare Administrative Contractors enter clinical and demographic information and subject claims to automated screening processes (MCE) to identify cases requiring further review; after screening, each claim is classified into an MS-LTC-DRG by the GROUPER software based on diagnosis/procedure codes and demographic info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GROUPER is the same program used under IPPS; some procedure codes are not recognized by GROUPER as affecting DRG assignment (minor/non-surgical procedures may not affect assignment); after GROUPER assignment, MAC determines prospective payment using PRICER and LTCHs have opportunity to review MS-LTC-DRG assignments and submit additional information within the timeframe provided in §412.513(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of MedPAR and GROUPER outputs to recalibrate relative weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Records for all Medicare hospital inpatient discharges are maintained in the MedPAR file and used to evaluate possible MS-DRG/MS-LTC-DRG classification changes and to recalibrate relative weights during annual updates under IPPS (§412.60(e)) and LTCH PPS (§412.517).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GROUPER is used both to classify past cases (to measure resource consumption for weight setting) and to classify current cases for payment determination; PRICER applies hospital-specific adjustments to determine prospective payment.
